Re-derived the complete differential adjoint p0,p1,p2 from (3-D)^j. On (0,a) its scalar derivative bounds follow from Delta_bar=Q D^2+(D Q-3Q)D. On [a,L] the accepted combined mixed bound retains the cancellation at the true bolt; separately divergent primitives are never estimated there.

The mixed moment Cmu bounds the entire finite interval by the polynomial coefficient sum and the actual scalar L2 energy. The R_b contribution integrates z^7 after squaring the weighted point bound, giving a^4/sqrt(88). The two R_J integrals give a^(3/2)/sqrt(3) and a^(7/2)/sqrt(7).

The inverse York weighted energy is obtained on Dirichlet exhaustions by testing y/z^2. Its forcing zeroth terms cancel exactly. The potential >=5/z^2 leaves the positive coefficients one and two; Cauchy-Schwarz gives KVm=1+1/sqrt(3). Exhaustion limits agree with the retained unique auxiliary realization.

The singular positive adjoint profile is an auxiliary Green profile, not a form-admitted physical variation. Local Frobenius expansion plus positive Dirichlet exhaustion fixes its z^-2 leading coefficient and the original zero value at the bolt. The Q^(2/3) supersolution is positive and has nonnegative L_Y image, establishing v<=M.

The bolt-regular homogeneous solution vanishes linearly; the inverse-Q potential multiplied by that solution has finite limit. At zero v prime is O(z), allowing a higher z^5 log term. Consequently all z^2 energy boundary terms vanish.

Green Wronskian is minus five y3 at the outer end, hence integral psi A_Y T=5y3. Integration by parts contributes minus two thirds T4, and S4=-two thirds T4 minus one half the full adjoint integral. A pure quartic having zero local forcing does not remove its global moment.

The dual norm for that integral is sqrt(integral z^-2 vprime^2). It is not the z^2 energy norm. Selection of a point b in [a,2a] and integration of (vprime/z^4)prime=V0 v/z^4 supplies the missing outer weight, with the displayed Dv<242.010389.
